title: The neighbour peel was proved — but never iterated into a product
content: The hard half of the Lovász Local Lemma induction step is a lower bound on the neighbour-block survival probability $\mu[\bigcap_{j\in S_1} A_j^c \mid C] \ge \prod_{j\in S_1}(1-x_j)$. The sibling **denominator-step** entry proved the SINGLE move behind it: $(1-x)\cdot l \le \mu[A^c \cap B \mid C]$ from $l \le \mu[B\mid C]$ and $\mu[A \mid B\cap C] \le x$ — peeling one neighbour $A = A_k$ deflates the running survival bound $l$ by a factor $(1-x_k)$. Its docstring explicitly deferred the rest: *'a well-founded recursion on $|S_1|$, still to be assembled'*. This entry assembles it. `cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod` is a `Finset.induction` over the neighbour block $S$ that iterates the peel — one insertion, one peel — accumulating the product $\prod_{j\in S}(1-x_j)$. The capstone `cond_failure_le_x_prod` then feeds the assembled product into the induction-step entry's abstract invariant, turning its abstract denominator $d$ into the concrete $\prod(1-x_j)$.
mathContext: ∏_{j∈S}(1 − xⱼ) ≤ μ[⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ | C], by induction on S iterating (1 − xₖ)·l ≤ μ[Aₖᶜ ∩ B | C].
relatedConcepts: well-founded recursion on a finite block

title: The measure-theoretic setting: probability μ, events A, budgets x
content: The import line pulls in `LovaszLocalLemmaOQ01InductionStep`, which transitively carries the single-neighbour peel `mul_one_sub_le_cond_compl` (from the denominator-step entry) and the abstract ratio invariant `cond_failure_le_x` (from the induction-step entry) — so this file needs no fresh probabilistic lemmas, only their composition. The `open` block brings `MeasureTheory`, `ProbabilityTheory`, `Finset`, the `ENNReal` scope, and the two OQ-01 namespaces into scope, so `cond`, `IndepSet`, `prod_insert`, and `set_biInter_insert` are all unqualified. The ambient context fixes an arbitrary measurable space $\Omega$ carrying a probability measure $\mu$ (`IsProbabilityMeasure μ`), a countable family of events $A : \mathbb{N} \to \text{Set }\Omega$, a fixed conditioning set $C$, and a budget function $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{\infty}$. Working in $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{\infty}$ (`ENNReal`) rather than $[0,1]$ is deliberate: conditional probabilities and their products live natively there, so `ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel` and `measure_ne_top` discharge the base case without side-casts.
mathContext: Ω measurable, μ a probability measure; A : ℕ → Set Ω the events, C the conditioning set, x : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞ the LLL budgets. All conditionals valued in ENNReal.

title: Statement and base case: the empty block gives μ[univ | C] = 1 = ∏_∅
content:
`cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod` states $\prod_{j\in S}(1-x_j) \le \mu[ igcap_{j\in S} A_j^c \mid C]$ with two side conditions carried as hypotheses quantified over **all** sub-blocks $T \subseteq S$: positivity of every partial history ($\mu[( igcap_{j\in T} A_j^c)\cap C] 
e 0$) and a per-event failure bound ($\mu[A_k \mid ( igcap_{j\in T} A_j^c)\cap C] \le x_k$ for $k\in S$, $T\subseteq S$, $k
otin T$). Quantifying over sub-blocks — not just $S$ — is what lets the induction hypothesis inherit exactly the bounds it needs at the smaller block. The proof is `Finset.induction_on S`. **Base $S=\varnothing$:** `hbi` rewrites $ igcap_{j\in\varnothing} A_j^c = 	ext{univ}$ by `simp`; the positivity hypothesis at $T=\varnothing$ then yields $\mu C 
e 0$ (after `Set.univ_inter`); and `cond_apply hC` unfolds $\mu[	ext{univ}\mid C] = (\mu C)^{-1}\cdot\mu(C\cap	ext{univ})$, which `Set.inter_univ` and `ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel` (using $\mu C 
e 0$ and $\mu C 
e \infty$ from `measure_ne_top`) collapse to $1$ — matching `Finset.prod_empty` $= 1$. With no neighbours to avoid, the survival lower bound is vacuously the empty product.
mathContext: Base: ⋂_{j∈∅} Aⱼᶜ = univ ⇒ goal 1 ≤ μ[univ | C]; cond_apply hC + Set.inter_univ + ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel (μ C ≠ 0, ≠ ∞) give μ[univ | C] = 1 = ∏_∅.

title: The insert step: one peel advances the block by one neighbour
content: The `insert a s` case ($a \notin s$) is where the peel is iterated. First the side conditions are **restricted** from $\text{insert } a\, s$ down to $s$ via `Finset.subset_insert` (giving `hpos'`, `hbound'`), so the induction hypothesis `ih` fires to yield $\text{IH} : \prod_{s}(1-x_j) \le \mu[\bigcap_{s} A_j^c \mid C]$. Then both sides are factored along the new neighbour $a$: `Finset.prod_insert ha` splits the product as $(1-x_a)\cdot\prod_{s}$, and `Finset.set_biInter_insert a s` splits the survival set as $A_a^c \cap \bigcap_{s} A_j^c$. The identity $A_a^c \cap \bigcap_{s} A_j^c = \bigcap_{\text{insert } a\, s} A_j^c$ is precisely why one peel advances the block by one element. Finally, a single `mul_one_sub_le_cond_compl` — fed measurability of $\bigcap_s A_j^c$ (`Finset.measurableSet_biInter`), the partial-history positivity `hBC = hpos s`, the per-event bound `hxa` at $a$ over history $s$, and IH — closes the goal to exactly $(1-x_a)\cdot\prod_s \le \mu[A_a^c \cap \bigcap_s A_j^c \mid C]$. That is the single-neighbour peel, now compounded once per insertion into the full product.
mathContext: Step: prod_insert ⇒ (1 − xₐ)·∏_s; set_biInter_insert ⇒ (A a)ᶜ ∩ ⋂_s Aⱼᶜ = ⋂_{insert a s} Aⱼᶜ; one mul_one_sub_le_cond_compl on IH closes (1 − xₐ)·∏_s ≤ μ[(A a)ᶜ ∩ ⋂_s Aⱼᶜ | C].

title: Threading the product into the invariant: the abstract d becomes ∏(1 − xⱼ)
content: `cond_failure_le_x_prod` is the payoff. The induction-step entry proved the invariant $\mu[A_i \mid N\cap C] \le x_i$ closes *once a denominator lower bound $d \le \mu[N\mid C]$ is supplied*, but left $d$ abstract. Here $d$ becomes concrete: set $C = \bigcap_{j\in S_2} A_j^c$ (measurable via `Finset.measurableSet_biInter`), obtain $\prod_{j\in S_1}(1-x_j) \le \mu[\bigcap_{j\in S_1} A_j^c \mid \bigcap_{j\in S_2} A_j^c]$ from `cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod`, and hand it to `cond_failure_le_x` as the denominator bound. Under the asymmetric LLL budget $\mu(A_i) \le x_i\cdot\prod_{j\in S_1}(1-x_j)$ and the non-neighbour independence $\text{IndepSet}\,A_i\,(\bigcap_{S_2} A_j^c)\,\mu$, the result is $\mu[A_i \mid (\bigcap_{S_1} A_j^c)\cap(\bigcap_{S_2} A_j^c)] \le x_i$ — the maintained invariant, now with the denominator equal to the actual product the textbook proof threads. **Honest scope:** the per-event bounds this consumes are themselves instances of the same invariant at smaller conditioning sets; the two directions form the Erdős–Lovász mutual recursion, and closing that mutual loop into an unconditional LLL is the remaining open OQ-01 target.
mathContext: cond_failure_le_x with d := ∏_{S₁}(1 − xⱼ) supplied by the recursion ⇒ μ[Aᵢ | (⋂_{S₁} Aⱼᶜ) ∩ (⋂_{S₂} Aⱼᶜ)] ≤ xᵢ.
